data_origin: Own controlled small-molecule ensemble inference using six frozen 1,4-butanediol conformers. RDKit ETKDGv3 seed57 generated a candidate pool; MMFF94 optimization supplies potential energies only. Selected original conformer indices0,1,2,3,5,6were rounded to0.001angstrom and frozen. This finite library, all synthetic spectroscopic observations and common-scale model are explicit benchmark assumptions, not an experimental conformer population, complete thermodynamic landscape or validated solution-state model.

structure_inputs.identity: SDF record0..5corresponds exactly toK1..K6; conformer_id and MMFF94_potential_kcalmol are record properties. Every record and every PDB has the same16explicit atoms in the same order. PDB atom serials are1based, scientific atom indices here are ZERO-based. Geometry is rounded identically in both formats; retain supplied coordinates and all parsed hydrogens. Re-embedding a shared SMILES or optimizing coordinates again changes the problem. PDB parser float precision is acceptable within reporting tolerances.

geometry_audit: First compare the SIX ACTUAL supplied SDF conformer geometries using USRCAT/GetUSRScore with conformer_policy=preserve,hydrogen_policy=as_parsed,optimization=none. Report the off-diagonal most-similar pair, naming its lower conformer ID first, and score. Do not mistake six copies of one regenerated canonical conformer for a coordinate-preserving comparison. A high global shape score does not guarantee equality of local proton-distance observables.
coupling_geometry: The central heavy-atom torsion uses atom indices[1,2,3,4] in that order. For each conformer phi is the conventional signed dihedral; only cos(phi) is needed. Compute J(phi)=9*cos(phi)^2-cos(phi)+0.5 in Hz. Its fixed coefficients and use of this heavy-atom torsion are controlled response assumptions. Coordinates/distances determine J before population fitting; J of an averaged geometry is not the ensemble-averaged coupling. All six interatomic distances within the four-atom set suffice to reconstruct cos(phi) without an arbitrary sign convention.
ideal_NOE_model: For a declared assigned proton pair(i,j), conformer response C_k=1000*(r_ij,k/angstrom)^(-6). Observed ideal intensity y=tau*sum_k p_k*C_k. p_k>=0,sum p=1 and one COMMON positive tau in[0.5,2]apply to every current and prospective NOE channel. tau is a dimensionless calibrated scale in this model; it is not independently fitted per pair or an experimentally estimated tumbling time. Assume this ideal r^-6ensemble average and no competing relaxation corrections by construction. Do not average distances first or mix complex amplitudes. Proton identities/assignments are fixed; swapping equivalent-looking hydrogen indices changes the supplied observable.

current_observations.uncertainty: Treat current observations as exact within numerical precision. The mixture J is sum p_k*J_k with NO tau factor.

identified_set_question: Use ALL current observations, positivity, normalization and shared scale. Report the rank of the complete linear equality system in[p_K1,..,p_K6,U]with U=1/tau, the SHARP marginal interval of every p_k, and the sharp tau interval. Define compact conformers by the ACTUAL proton distance r(7,13)<3angstrom and report their IDs and sharp total population interval. All endpoint claims require global optimality and feasible witnesses. A single least-squares, maximum-entropy or minimum-energy mixture is not proof of a unique population. Decide whether the marginal intervals form an independently selectable Cartesian joint feasible box; retain the coupled constraints.

prospective_probe_design.hypotheses: H_high means compact population>=0.50; H_low means compact population<=0.15. Both use the ENTIRE coupled current-data feasible set and shared tau. They are deliberately separated hypotheses, not an exhaustive division of all feasible mixtures. Do not assume the actual ensemble belongs to one of them.
prospective_probe_design.criterion: For each probe compute its complete ideal intensity interval under each hypothesis, allowing populations AND the common scale to vary together subject to ALL existing observations. Raw interval gap=max(0,L_high-U_low,L_low-U_high). Positive raw gap alone is insufficient: future observed intensity intervals are each widened by0.05on both sides. Guaranteed discrimination requires raw gap STRICTLY greater than0.10; equality fails. Choose the lowest-cost probe meeting this criterion, breaking remaining ties by numeric probe ID. Report all raw-gap-positive and all noise-robust probe IDs separately. No actual follow-up observation is supplied, so do not infer which separated hypothesis is true.

potential_energy_control: Read the actual SDF potential energies and form a NAIVE unit-degeneracy Boltzmann population at298.15K, R=0.00198720425864083kcal/(mol*K), using relative energies. Report this six-entry population inK1..K6order, and whether it satisfies ALL current NOE/J observations with one tau in[0.5,2]. This is a test of an explicitly proposed potential-energy approximation; MMFF94 potential energies are NOT automatically conformer free energies or state entropies. Do not use this population as hidden truth when deriving identified bounds.

interpretation_proposals.A: The ideal NOE response averages inverse sixth powers at fixed proton identity, not the sixth inverse power of the mean distance.
interpretation_proposals.B: Six records sharing a molecular graph may be replaced by six copies of one regenerated geometry without changing the supplied ensemble problem.
interpretation_proposals.C: Common-scale uncertainty must remain coupled to populations when bounding an unmeasured probe.
interpretation_proposals.D: Any positive raw separation guarantees discrimination under the stated nonzero future error bounds.
interpretation_proposals.E: Marginal population bounds and one fitted mixture do not by themselves specify a unique joint ensemble.
interpretation_proposals.F: The two separated compact-population hypotheses exhaust all scientifically possible ensembles supported by the current data.
interpretation_proposals.G: A molecular mechanics potential-energy Boltzmann distribution is a proposed prior/model control, not a measured solution-state population.

reporting: Return actual_SDF_most_similar_conformer_pair,actual_SDF_USRCAT_similarity; conformer_J_Hz keyedK1..K6; compact_conformer_ids sorted; population_scale_equality_rank integer; identified_population_intervals_by_conformer keyedK1..K6; identified_tau_interval; identified_compact_population_interval; marginal_intervals_are_independent_joint_box boolean; prospective_intensity_intervals_by_probe_and_hypothesis keyedP1..P5thenH_high,H_low; raw_positive_gap_probe_ids sorted; noise_robust_probe_ids sorted; selected_probe_id; naive_MMFF_Boltzmann_populations as six numbers; naive_MMFF_ensemble_satisfies_all_current_observations boolean; valid_interpretation_proposal_ids sorted. IDs, rank and booleans exact. Shape score absolute1e-7. J and optimized bounds absolute2e-4plus relative1e-5 to allow PDB parser precision; naive Boltzmann populations absolute1e-7plus relative1e-6. Probabilities remain physical and endpoint ordering matters. Keep global completeness and endpoint evidence in the trajectory instead of listing every feasible mixture.

methodological_sources.title: Assessing the effect of conformational averaging on the measured values of observables
methodological_sources.role: Primary methods motivation for joint NOE/J ensemble inference. No measurement data or peptide sequences copied; this problem is a fixed benign small-molecule controlled model.

methodological_sources.title: RDKit USRCAT conformer geometry descriptors
methodological_sources.role: Primary software documentation for the explicitly declared global shape comparison; it does not convert a shape score into experimental ensemble evidence.
